title: Code Execution Sandbox Pricing 2026: Cost, Cold Starts, and Persistence for AI Agents
keyword: code execution sandbox pricing AI agents

competitors.name: E2B

tiers.name: Hobby
tiers.limits: 1-hour max sandbox session, 20 concurrent sandboxes, 10 GiB storage free

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 24-hour max sandbox session, 100 concurrent sandboxes (up to 1,100 purchasable), 20 GiB storage free

competitors.cold_start: Sub-second cold start for sandboxes; sandboxes are lightweight VMs that boot quickly
competitors.persistence: Sandbox sessions up to 1 hour (Hobby) or 24 hours (Pro); no persistent filesystem across sessions by default
competitors.target_audience: AI agents needing secure, isolated code execution environments
strengths: Purpose-built for AI agent code execution
Per-second billing means no idle cost
weaknesses: Pro tier at $150/month is relatively expensive for small teams
Session length limits may be restrictive for long-running agents
No GPU support mentioned in standard tiers

competitors.name: Modal
competitors.pricing_model: Pure per-second billing, no subscription tiers

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 3 workspace seats, 100 containers + 10 GPU concurrency, limited scheduled/Web Functions

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Unlimited seats, higher concurrency, SSO, priority support

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Dedicated capacity, custom contracts, advanced security

competitors.cold_start: Sub-second cold starts for CPU functions; GPU functions may take 5-15 seconds for model loading; container pooling available
competitors.persistence: Volumes for persistent storage ($0.09/GiB/month); functions are stateless by default; scheduled functions keep warm
competitors.target_audience: AI/ML teams needing serverless GPU and CPU compute
strengths: No subscription fees — pay only for compute used
Wide GPU selection including latest B300/B200
weaknesses: No dedicated sandbox isolation model (runs as containers)
Cold starts on GPU can be significant
Less suited for persistent agent sessions vs. stateless functions

competitors.name: Fly.io

usage_costs.gpu: Available but pricing not publicly listed on standard page

competitors.cold_start: Suspend/resume model: stopped VMs resume in ~100-500ms; cold start from scratch ~1-3 seconds
competitors.persistence: Volumes for persistent storage; VMs can be suspended (not destroyed) preserving state; 6GB ephemeral storage included
competitors.target_audience: Developers needing global edge deployment with simple VM management
strengths: Extremely cheap for low-usage scenarios ($0.0028/hr for smallest VM)
Suspend/resume eliminates cold start for frequently-used VMs
weaknesses: Not purpose-built for AI agent code execution
No built-in sandbox isolation for untrusted code
GPU options limited and not transparently priced
Less suited for ephemeral agent tasks vs. long-running services

key_trends: Per-second billing is the dominant model across all major sandbox providers
AI agent sandbox market is rapidly growing with E2B leading the purpose-built segment
Cold start optimization is a key differentiator — sub-second targets are now standard
GPU compute for AI agents is becoming table stakes (Modal leads with widest GPU selection)
Free tiers with usage credits are the standard acquisition model

pricing_comparison_gpu_h100_per_second.Fly.io: GPU available but pricing not public

persistence_comparison.E2B: Session-based (1-24h), no cross-session persistence by default
persistence_comparison.Fly.io: Volumes + suspend/resume preserves VM state, 6GB ephemeral
